RdRP and RNA polymerases are structurally related and that this relationship is the result of an evolutionary process.

RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRPs) have evolved from DNA-dependent RNA polymerase.

The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA silencing is a transcription process, and it is the same as DNA transcription, but the DNA is replaced by RNA.
RNA silencing in eukaryotes may have evolved from the transcription apparatus of an RNA-based organism.
RdRP enzymes, which have long been considered to be distinct from DNA-dependent RNA polymerase enzymes, actually have the same overall structure and share a common evolutionary origin.
